Phonetic-Aware Letter-Based Next Word Pr.description: Over a billion South Asian users type their languages in Latin script on English keyboards, but autocomplete serves them poorly: suggestions only appear once a word is complete, valid spelling variants are treated as different words, and code-mixed sentences confuse single-language models. This project builds a single on-device model for Hindi-, Urdu-, Bangla- and Tamil-English transliterated typing that predicts after every keystroke, uses phonetic matching (weighted edit distance over sound and consonant patterns) to treat spelling variants as equivalent, and ranks top-K suggestions by context. Lightweight text commands (e.g. ?fix, ?formal, ?shorten, ?translate) extend it beyond autocomplete.

KGNode v2: Self-Tuning Agentic Framework.description: KGNode is a training-free knowledge-graph question answering pipeline evaluated on DBLP-QuAD and QALD-10. Version 2 turns it into a self-optimising agentic system: a LangGraph workflow with quality gates that stop early on poor intermediate results, DSPy-driven prompt optimisation for entity extraction, template generation and SPARQL synthesis, and automatic hyperparameter adaptation to the query and the KG. The system is packaged as an MCP server and evaluated against v1 on accuracy, runtime and cross-domain transfer, with ablations per component.

deliverables: Data and problem analysis: identify realistic EHR prediction tasks (e.g. risk, length of stay, readmission) and gaps in recent multimodal healthcare literature.
A multimodal model combining two or more modalities; comparison of fusion strategies (early/late fusion, cross-attention, contrastive learning), optionally with pretrained clinical models.
Interpretability: attention analysis, feature attribution and modality-contribution analysis that a clinician could follow.
Evaluation with AUROC, AUPRC and calibration, plus modality ablations, and a critical discussion of limitations.
prerequisites: Strong motivation to apply AI/ML to healthcare
Good Python and deep learning skills
Familiarity with transformers or sequence models; basic NLP, time-series or computer vision knowledge
